02 / The service

Make the essentials easy to read.

Van signwriting gives people a quick way to recognise your business and know who to call. At our Norwich workshop, we design, produce and fit cut vinyl lettering and printed van graphics for tradespeople, local deliveries and service businesses across Norfolk. It works on everything from a compact service van with a logo and phone number to a long-wheelbase van with a larger design across both sides and the rear.

Start with the details you want someone to read at a glance. Your business name, main service and one contact detail usually give the design a clear order. We lay the artwork out around handles, recesses and door joins, taking the original paint colour into account. If your logo needs several colours or contains a gradient, we can discuss printing it as a graphic instead of building it from separate colours of cut film.

Send the make, model, year and photos of each side. We can advise on coverage, show you a proof and arrange fitting in Norwich after you approve the design.

08 / Vinyl & materials

Choose the right film.

Cut lettering suits simple colours and shapes. Printed film can reproduce complex logos or gradients. Specify the finish against the body colour, including how it reads under overcast light.

Cast vs calendered
Cast vinyl conforms to more complex bodywork. Suitable calendered film can work on flatter areas and simpler curves. The exact product and surface determine suitability.
Brands used
3M and Metamark are examples to discuss. Ask for the product and finish on your quote.
Lifespan
Film, panel angle, care and exposure all matter. As one product example, 3M 2080 lists up to eight years on qualifying vertical applications and up to three on horizontal applications. Check the applicable product terms.
Finishes
Ask about gloss, matt, satin, chrome-effect or reflective film. Speciality finishes can have different fitting, care and durability requirements.

15 / FAQ

Good to know.

What should I put on my van?

Start with your business name, what you do and the contact detail you want customers to use. Your logo, colours and website can help tie it to your other branding.

Can you work from my own artwork?

Yes. Share what you have when you enquire. A vector logo is useful if available, and we can discuss what needs preparing before production.

What is the difference between cut vinyl and printed graphics?

Cut vinyl uses shapes and letters cut from a coloured film. Printed graphics can reproduce gradients, photos and more complex branding.

Can I signwrite just the rear doors?

Yes. Tell us which panels you want covered. A rear-only design can focus on a phone number, website or short trade description.

How should I prepare my van?

Tell us about wax, coatings, existing stickers and paint repairs before the fitting. Follow the workshop’s preparation instructions when confirming your slot.

Can old lettering be removed first?

Send photos of the existing film and the paint around it. Removal and any adhesive cleanup can be priced separately after inspection.

Can you add my logo to a coloured van?

Yes. We can check contrast against the actual body colour and advise on a suitable film or a backing panel if the logo needs it.

Do you offer graphics for one van?

Yes. A single work van can be quoted and fitted in Norwich. Tell us which sides and doors you want to use.

Will I see the design before fitting?

Yes. Review the layout on a proof and check your contact details, colours and artwork placement before approving it.

Can signwriting be removed before a lease return?

Ask the lease provider first. Film can generally be removed professionally, with the result depending on the paint condition, film and its age.
